description.comment: Layer peritonitis is considered a major cause of morbidity and mortality in laying hens which leads to significant economic losses to the table egg industry worldwide. Escherichia coli is the most common bacterial species associated with layer peritonitis. Despite its importance to the poultry industry, pathogenesis of layer peritonitis has not been elucidated. The objectives of the current study are; 1) to identify potential virulence factors encoded in E. coli causing peritonitis using whole genome sequencing, 2) ascertain genotypic homology among avian pathogenic E. coli and human extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli by comparative genomics, and 3) to identify potential vaccine targets through antigenome approaches

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli strain:ATCC 700415 Genome sequencing and assembly

description.comment: Escherichia coli strain ATCC 700415 is a naturally occurring, Gram-negative, enteric bacterium that was isolated from a woman with cystitis (bladder infection). This strain possesses virulence factors consistent with Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC). Urinary tract infections could be considered a form of foodborne illness, as meat and poultry are routinely contaminated with UPEC. Urinary tract infections can occur after consumption of contaminated food, colonization of the distal colon by UPEC, followed by accidental transfer of contaminated feces from the anus to the urethra. In this study, we fully sequenced and annotated Escherichia coli ATCC 700415 to further elucidate the genome and to facilitate research on the detection and control of UPEC in foods.

description.comment: Layer peritonitis is considered a major cause of morbidity and mortality in laying hens which leads to significant economic losses to the table egg industry worldwide. Escherichia coli is the most common bacterial species associated with layer peritonitis. Despite its importance to the poultry industry, pathogenesis of layer peritonitis has not been elucidated. The objectives of the current study are; 1) to identify potential virulence factors encoded in E. coli causing peritonitis using whole genome sequencing, 2) ascertain genotypic homology among avian pathogenic E. coli and human extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli by comparative genomics, and 3) to identify potential vaccine targets through antigenome approaches

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli str. RM10466 Genome sequencing and assembly

description.comment: The rise in foodborne-related outbreaks of non O157 shiga-toxin producing E. coli (STECs) emphasizes the importance of developing improved methods to rapidly detect and characterize STECs. The major serovars of STEC associated with illness have been O26, O111, O103, O121, O113, O43, and O145, accounting for 25-50% of human illness caused by STECs and, in some cases, severe illness comparable to illness caused by E. coli O157:H7. Sequencing of STECs from the agriculturally important region of the California central coast will address the diversity of genomic content and physiology of STECs compared to E. coli O157.

bioprojects.title: The strategy of a novel way to enhance bacterial motility

description.comment: To date, only a few studies identified hyper-motile isolates that affect FlhDC at the post-translational level. Here we obtained this kind of hyper-motile isolates by evolving an E. coli K12 NCM3722 wild-type strain (CY598) on the soft agar plate. These isolates shared one single point mutation in ClpX, making ClpX another hot locus during evolution of bacterial motility. We then revealed the molecular mechanism of the ClpX mutant mediated FlhDC accumulation and reasoned the trade-off between motility and growth at the molecular level for the first time.
description.title: ClpXV78F mediated FlhDC accumulation bursts motility of Escherichia coli

bioprojects.title: Complete genome sequence of Escherichia coli K-12 substrain AB1157, the preferred strain for the DNA metabolism studies

description.comment: AB1157 was isolated in the lab of Edward A. Adelberg, and became the reference strain for Paul Howard-Flanders genetic studies of DNA replication, damage, and repair. An early pioneer in DNA studies, Howard-Flanders favored the strain for its lack of prophage induction and consequent genetic stability under elevated levels of genotoxic stress. To date, AB1157 is still frequently employed as an E. coli reference strain by researchers worldwide.

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli strain:48 Genome sequencing

description.comment: Shiga toxin (Stx)-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) are important foodborne enteric pathogens that cause gastrointestinal illnesses and potentially fatal sequelae including haemolytic-ureamic syndrome (HUS). Ruminants including cattle are important STEC reservoirs. In addition to shigatoxins, some STEC strains also produce the cytotoxin subtilase (SubAB) . STEC isolate 48 originating from a roe deer although positive in the primary subAB screening yielded negative results upon subtyping the subAB-variants. Our goal in the present study was to determine the draft genome of STEC isolate 48 and define the genetic environment of the subAB gene locus in this strain.

bioprojects.title: We developed a theoretical framework which explains why the relationship between growth rate (r) and carrying capacity (K) describes a skew parabola, and applied this parabola to the study of of antibiotic resistance. We demonstrate that, to become resistant, microbes need not to increase r at the cost of K (costs of resistance) but, upon abundance of nutrients, the presence of an antibiotic can lead to an increase in r and K creating a `uberbug'.

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli C strain:C Genome sequencing and assembly

description.comment: Escherichia coli is a model prokaryote and a key organism for laboratory and industrial applications. E. coli strain C was isolated at the Lister Institute and deposited into the National Collection of Type Cultures, London in 1920 (Strain No. 122). It was characterized as more spherical than other strains and its nuclear matter is peripherally distributed in the cell (Lieb et al. 1955). E. coli C, called a restrictionless strain, has been used for bacteriophage studies since early 50s (Bertani and Weigle 1953). Genetic tests showed that E. coli C forms an O rough R1-type lipopolysaccharide which serve as receptor for bacteriophages (Feige and Stirm 1976). Its genetic map showing similarities to E. coli K12 strain was constructed in 1970 (Wiman et al. 1970).

description.comment: The rise in foodborne-related outbreaks of non O157 shiga-toxin producing E. coli (STECs) emphasizes the importance of developing improved methods to rapidly detect and characterize STECs. The major serovars of STEC associated with illness have been O26, O111, O103, O121, O43, and O145, accounting for 25-50% of human illness caused by STECs and, in some cases, severe illness comparable to illness caused by E. coli O157:H7. Sequencing of STECs from the agriculturally important region of the California central coast will address the diversity of genomic content and physiology of STECs compared to E. coli O157.

description.comment: The rise in foodborne-related outbreaks of non O157 shiga-toxin producing E. coli (STECs) emphasizes the importance of developing improved methods to rapidly detect and characterize STECs. The major serovars of STEC associated with illness have been O26, O111, O103, O121, O43, and O145, accounting for 25-50% of human illness caused by STECs and, in some cases, severe illness comparable to illness caused by E. coli O157:H7. Sequencing of STECs from the agriculturally important region of the California central coast will address the diversity of genomic content and physiology of STECs compared to E. coli O157.

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli O145 str. RM9872 genome sequencing

description.comment: The rise in foodborne-related outbreaks of non O157 shiga-toxin producing E. coli (STECs) emphasizes the importance of developing improved methods to rapidly detect and characterize STECs. The major serovars of STEC associated with illness have been O26, O111, O103, O121, O43, and O145, accounting for 25-50% of human illness caused by STECs and, in some cases, severe illness comparable to illness caused by E. coli O157:H7. Sequencing of STECs from the agriculturally important region of the California central coast will address the diversity of genomic content and physiology of STECs compared to E. coli O157.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: typical patient during the Sakai outbreak

description.comment: Full genome sequenced type strain Escherichia coli O157:H7 str. SAKAI.  This strain is associated with Hamburger disease, which is caused by the contamination of meat products by enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC). The identifier O157:H7 refers to the serotype of EHEC, and reflects the specific antigenic markers found on the surface of the cell. EHEC attaches and effaces to cells in the large intestine.There are numerous differences that distinguish O157:H7 from K-12, hundreds of them associated with genomic islands in either strain, including at least 9 large PAIs in O157:H7 that encode virulence factors. A type III secretion system, the locus of enterocyte effacement, numerous toxins and adhesins, as well as fimbrial gene clusters and iron uptake systems are found in these PAIs. Pathogenicity genes are also found on the plasmid pO157. Escherichia coli O157:H7 strain Sakai. This strain of O157:H7 was isolated in a 1996 outbreak in Sakai, Japan.

attributes.value: ESBL producer resistant to CAZ, CTX, AMC, CIP, SXT, RL (EUCAST guidelines)

description.comment: Strain Escherichia coli HK02 is a member of globally distributed clonal complex of ExPEC strain ST131. Laterally acquired antibiotic resistance gene blaCTX-M-15, located on the chromosome, is responsible for the ESBL phenotype, while point mutations in parC and gyrA regions confer resistance to ciprofloxacin. The strain showed resistance to amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, sulfamethoxazole, alone and in the combination with trimethoprim, which can be attributed to number of unspecific efflux pumps encoded by housekeeping genes. Production of ESBL enzymes and resistance to fluoroquinolones together with fimH30 allelic variation classify sequenced isolate as a member of H30Rx clade. Since there are no specific virulence factors strictly connected with ExPEC pathotype, the strain is classified based on the genetic similarity with the known, infection-causing, strains. The isolate is identified as a human pathogen, associated with blood stream and urinary tract infections (UTIs), acquired in both, community and in hospital settings.

bioprojects.title: Escherichia coli O26 str. RM10386 genome sequencing

description.comment: The rise in foodborne-related outbreaks of non O157 shiga-toxin producing E. coli (STECs) emphasizes the importance of developing improved methods to rapidly detect and characterize STECs. The major serovars of STEC associated with illness have been O26, O111, O103, O121, O43, and O145, accounting for 25-50% of human illness caused by STECs and, in some cases, severe illness comparable to illness caused by E. coli O157:H7. Sequencing of STECs from the agriculturally important region of the California central coast will address the diversity of genomic content and physiology of STECs compared to E. coli O157.
